LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 SELF- EXPRESSION: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Self- expression: Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Self- expression: Pronunciation, part of Strand 4 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to observe punctuation marks in self-expression?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify punctuation marks for accurate articulation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Self- expression: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use correct pronunciation and pauses in sentences for self-expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Self- expression: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate punctuation for accurate pronunciation in self- expression.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Self- expression: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is developed as the learner pronounces words, sentences and phrases

accurately in a variety of contexts.

• Self- efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner shows concerted attention when discussing various punctuation marks

and how they affect pronunciation of words, sentences and phrases.

Values:
● Respect: This is acquired as the learner appreciates each other’s opinion when discussing different punctuation marks.

● Love: This is developed as the learner assists peers to acquire good pronunciation when peer reviewing each other’s

presentation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

ICT: This is promoted as the learner embraces technology when teaming up to record themselves reading

paragraphs aloud using correct pronunciation and pauses.

Link to other subjects:

The learner can apply the concept of pronunciation to their learning in English.
